posts.author: John Sonley
posts.content_md:
I am planning to make a 10 inch plano convex lens with a focal length of about 12 inches using Bonda casting resin - polymerised styrene.

Has anyone attempted this before and can you give me practical guidance as to a suitable mold and cooling to prevent thermal cracking during the polymerisation. I am aware of the toxic nature of styrene

posts.author: Tom B.
posts.content_md:
Some hints in this FAQ: [http://users.lmi.net/~drewid/resin_faq.html](http://users.lmi.net/~drewid/resin_faq.html)

Optical casting looks tricky 

Are you making a cylinder or a spherical lens?

posts.author: Martin
posts.content_md:
> **John Sonley:** I am planning to make a 10 inch plano convex lens with a focal length of about 12 inches using Bonda casting resin - polymerised styrene.Has anyone attempted this before and can you give me practical guidance as to a suitable mold and cooling to prevent thermal cracking during the polymerisation. I am aware of the toxic nature of styrene

I found styrene based resins very messy (to say the least) to work with: cooling thick layers turned out to be awkward to control. In addition cracks may form due to local heating. Regarding the health risks the polymerized stuff may keep releasing styrene for several months.

You might consider a liquid lens. Vidar Hegdal, who used to post here, seems to have made good experiences with liquid lenses. See: [http://www.techsoft.no/holography/lenses.htm](http://www.techsoft.no/holography/lenses.htm)

posts.author: Tommy
posts.content_md:

posts.author: edelbrp
posts.content_md:
> **Martin:** You might consider a liquid lens. Vidar Hegdal, who used to post here, seems to have made good experiences with liquid lenses. See:http://www.techsoft.no/holography/lenses.htm

Ditto on the liquid lens. I've made large water-filled prisms with some pieces of glass and aquarium glue. Worse case is you'll have a leak and need a little more glue. I don't think I would bother with oil or anything messy like that. Water is probably just fine for most applications.

BTW-I'm not sure where to get (or make) large curved plexi or glass with precision. Any ideas?

-Phil

posts.author: Martin
posts.content_md:
> **edelbrp:** Ditto on the liquid lens. I've made large water-filled prisms with some pieces of glass and aquarium glue. Worse case is you'll have a leak and need a little more glue. I don't think I would bother with oil or anything messy like that. Water is probably just fine for most applications.

Due to the higher refractive index, organic liquids may have the advantage of providing considerably shorter focal lengths though.

If I were to make once more that kind of large lenses, I would also look into the possibility of using Candle Jelly. It is based on (non-toxic) PIB (polyisobutylene).
